name: File OEB Reporting and Record-keeping Requirements (RRR) returns and the scorecard MD&A
summary: The Ontario Energy Board requires every licensed distributor to file about twenty returns a year under its Reporting and Record-keeping Requirements: most are due on April 30 (audited statements, uniform-system-of-accounts trial balance, service quality and reliability, customer arrears, assistance programs, scorecard measures), with a market summary in February, quarterly generation connection data and the scorecard commentary later in the year. A regulatory analyst runs each return, collecting data from accounting, billing and the outage system, checking it against prior years, keying it into the OEB portal and getting it certified. It is slow because data owners give it low priority and financial returns wait for the audit, and error-prone because figures are re-keyed from several systems and must agree across returns.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 350,000 customers and a small regulatory affairs team.
baseline.notes: Requirements as revised March 31, 2020. Several returns (2.1.1 and a scorecard measure) were removed during the period.

unit_of_work: one RRR return (one section due on one deadline, or the scorecard MD&A)
trigger: A deadline in the RRR compliance calendar approaches and the source data for the period (audited statements, year-end customer counts, interruption records) is available.
end_state: The return is submitted and certified in the OEB portal, and any OEB follow-up query is answered or the data revised.

volume.seasonality: Strongly seasonal: about fifteen of the roughly twenty-one returns are due on April 30, one at the end of February, quarterly generation data at the end of February, May, August and November, and the scorecard MD&A in late summer.

evidence.note: Count of distributor reporting sections and deadlines in s1 (about 21 a year); MD&A timing from s2. High case allows for ad hoc reports (2.1.18, 2.1.21) and data revisions.
Regulatory analysts own RRR returns (s1 lists the sections); FTE share estimated.
Reviews each return before filing; share estimated.
Prepares financial, USoA and deferral account returns after the audit; share estimated.
Runs CIS reports for customer, arrears, disconnection and assistance program counts. Not listed in the organisation file's process entry.

roles.title: Vice-President (operations, engineering, customer service, finance, corporate services)
roles.department: Office of the President and CEO

evidence.note: Acts as RRR signing officer for the quarterly and annual certification (s1, 2.2.3).

roles.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
roles.department: Office of the President and CEO

systems.name: OEB RRR and regulatory e-filing portal
ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Contact centre telephony, IVR and call recording
Document management and engineering drawing repository

steps.name: Open the filing calendar item
steps.description: The regulatory analyst opens the RRR compliance calendar, sees which return is due and when, creates a working folder for this year's return and notes who owns the source data.

evidence.note: Deadlines from s1.

steps.name: Check filing guide changes and last year's return
steps.description: The analyst reads the OEB's current RRR filing guide and any letters changing the requirement, opens last year's filed return and working papers, and lists what is new, removed or redefined this year.

error.defect_description: A changed definition is missed and old logic is reused.

evidence.note: RRR requirements are revised over time; s2 notes a measure removed in 2021.

steps.name: Send data requests to data owners
steps.description: The analyst emails each data owner the template, definitions and due date for the figures needed. The path then depends on the kind of return: financial, customer, operational or the scorecard commentary.

next.condition: financial return (audited statements, trial balance, USoA, deferral accounts, PBR data)
customer return (arrears, disconnections, OESP, LEAP, market monitoring)
operational return (service quality, reliability, generation connections, cyber readiness)

evidence.note: Section mix from s1: about seven financial, five customer, seven operational returns and one MD&A a year.

steps.name: Extract trial balance and financial data from the ERP
steps.description: After the external audit closes, the accountant runs the year-end trial balance, the uniform system of accounts sub-ledgers, Group 1 deferral and variance account principal and interest, and labour and FTE figures, and saves them to the RRR template.

error.defect_description: Wrong period or account mapping used.

evidence.note: Contents of 2.1.5, 2.1.6 and 2.1.7 (s1); the wait for audit sign-off before April 30 is estimated.

steps.name: Map and reconcile USoA balances to the audited statements
steps.description: The accountant maps each ledger account to the OEB uniform system of accounts, reconciles the totals to the audited financial statements line by line and documents any reclassification so the return can be defended.

control.basis: OEB RRR 2.1.13: USoA balances mapped and reconciled to the audited financial statements

evidence.note: Requirement in s1 (2.1.13); effort estimated.

steps.name: Run CIS reports for customer statistics
steps.description: The billing analyst runs CIS queries for customers by class, accounts in arrears and arrears payment agreements, disconnections for non-payment, OESP and LEAP recipients, and retailer enrolments, and pastes the counts into the template.

error.defect_description: Query picks up the wrong date range or account status.

evidence.note: Data items from 2.1.2, 2.1.8, 2.1.9 and 2.1.16 (s1); effort estimated.

steps.name: Customer service manager reviews customer statistics
steps.description: The customer service manager compares the counts with internal monthly reports and last year's figures and approves them or sends back queries.

evidence.note: Typical owner sign-off; estimated.

steps.name: Extract interruptions and service quality data
steps.description: The asset analyst exports the year's interruptions from the OMS by month and cause code and computes customer-hours and customers interrupted, and collects the Distribution System Code service quality counts (connections, appointments, call answering, reconnections) from the CIS and telephony reports.

error.defect_description: Interruptions coded to the wrong cause or month, or a duplicate event.

evidence.note: Monthly reliability and service quality items in 2.1.4 (s1); effort estimated.

steps.name: Check major event exclusions and loss-of-supply events
steps.description: The analyst checks which days qualify as major events, separates loss of supply from the transmitter, and writes the required description of each major event and the actions taken, so that indices with and without them are reported correctly.

evidence.note: Major event reporting questions in 2.1.4 (s1).

steps.name: Load the data into the RRR template
steps.description: The analyst copies the figures from each data owner into the RRR return workbook or the portal upload template, checks units and signs, and fills in definitions and notes.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Run year-over-year and cross-section checks
steps.description: The analyst compares each figure with the last three years and with related returns (customer counts against the yearbook, financial statement totals against the trial balance, reliability against the scorecard) and flags any change beyond tolerance.

control.basis: OEB RRR 2.2.3: adequate processes and controls to ensure filed information is accurate

evidence.note: Control expectation in 2.2.3 (s1); variance share estimated.

steps.name: Query the data owner about a variance
steps.description: The analyst emails the data owner the flagged figures and waits for either an explanation to note in the return or corrected data.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Regulatory manager reviews the return
steps.description: The regulatory manager reads the return and the variance notes, checks consistency with rate filings and public statements, and approves it or sends it back.

evidence.note: Typical review; estimated.

steps.name: Enter the return in the OEB portal
steps.description: The analyst logs into the OEB RRR filing portal and keys or uploads each figure from the approved workbook, attaching documents such as the audited statements where required.

evidence.note: Manner and form prescribed by the OEB (s1, section 1.5).

steps.name: Portal runs validation rules
steps.description: The OEB portal checks required fields, totals and ranges and lists errors or warnings for the analyst to resolve before submission.

evidence.note: Typical portal behaviour; error share estimated.

steps.name: Fix portal validation errors
steps.description: The analyst reads each portal error, corrects the keyed figure or adds an explanation for a warning, and resubmits for validation.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Signing officer certifies the filing
steps.description: The vice-president acting as RRR signing officer (or the CEO for certifications that require the CEO) reviews the summary and signs the statement that the information is complete and accurate and that adequate controls are in place.

control.basis: OEB RRR 2.2.3 quarterly and annual certification by the CEO or RRR signing officer

evidence.note: Certification requirement in 2.2.3 (s1).

steps.name: Submit the return and file the confirmation
steps.description: The analyst submits the return in the portal, saves the confirmation and the working papers to the document store and marks the item complete in the compliance calendar.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Update the internal performance summary
steps.description: The analyst adds the filed figures to the internal regulatory performance summary that goes to the executive team and board, highlighting measures that missed their target.

evidence.note: Estimated; follow-up share estimated.

steps.name: OEB staff send a follow-up query
steps.description: OEB staff reviewing filings across distributors, or preparing the yearbook and scorecard, send a query about an outlier or an inconsistency between returns.

evidence.note: Typical compliance follow-up; frequency and timing estimated.

steps.name: Draft the scorecard MD&A commentary
steps.description: Once the OEB has populated the scorecard from the April filings, the analyst writes the management discussion and analysis for each measure (service quality, satisfaction, safety, reliability, asset management, cost control, financial ratios), explaining results, trends and actions.

error.defect_description: Commentary does not match the reported figures.

evidence.note: The 2021 scorecard MD&A runs to 11 pages and the scorecard is dated August 31, 2022 (s2); drafting effort and wait estimated.

steps.name: Executives review the MD&A
steps.description: The customer service manager and the vice-presidents responsible for each measure read the commentary for their area, correct facts and tone, and return comments to the analyst.

evidence.note: Typical review; estimated.

steps.name: CEO certifies the scorecard and MD&A
steps.description: The CEO reads the final scorecard and MD&A and signs the statement that the information is complete and accurate in all material respects.

control.basis: OEB RRR 2.2.2: CEO certification of the scorecard including the MD&A

evidence.note: Requirement in 2.2.2 (s1).

steps.name: Investigate the query and prepare a data revision
steps.description: The analyst goes back to the working papers and the data owner, decides whether the figure was wrong, and either explains it to OEB staff or prepares a data revision request with the corrected figures.
outputs: query response or data revision request

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Regulatory manager approves the data revision
steps.description: The regulatory manager checks the corrected figures against the working papers, reads the explanation for OEB staff, and approves resubmission through the portal's data revision process.

evidence.note: Estimated.

exceptions.name: Unexplained variance
exceptions.description: A figure moves beyond tolerance from last year and the analyst must query the owner and wait for an explanation or a correction.

exceptions.name: Portal validation errors
exceptions.description: The portal rejects totals or ranges and the analyst fixes and revalidates.

exceptions.name: OEB follow-up and data revision
exceptions.description: OEB staff question an outlier; about six in ten queries end in a data revision request and resubmission.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from opening the return to submission
benchmarks.population: One RRR return at a mid-size Ontario distributor

evidence.note: Author's estimate of working time inside the filing windows set by s1: about 120 days from year end to the April 30 deadline, and two months after quarter end for quarterly returns; financial returns cannot start until the audit closes.

pain_points.description: Financial returns cannot start until the audit closes, which squeezes the trial balance, USoA reconciliation and deferral account returns into the last weeks before April 30, when the month-end close is also running.

evidence.note: April 30 deadline for audited statements and reconciled USoA balances (s1); squeeze estimated.

pain_points.description: Figures are pulled from the ERP, CIS, OMS and telephony reports into spreadsheets and then re-keyed into the portal, so transcription errors and inconsistent definitions between returns are common.

evidence.note: Typical for the period; error rates estimated.

pain_points.description: Data owners in other departments treat RRR requests as low priority, so queries about variances wait days for answers.

evidence.note: Estimated.

sources.title: Electricity Reporting and Record Keeping Requirements (RRR), revised March 31, 2020
sources.supports: Distributor filing sections and deadlines: market monitoring summary by the end of February (2.1.2); about fifteen annual returns due April 30 (2.1.4 service quality and reliability by month, 2.1.5 performance-based regulation data including FTEs and regulated ROE, 2.1.6 audited financial statements, 2.1.7 trial balance in uniform system of accounts and Group 1 deferral and variance account balances, 2.1.8 arrears and disconnections, 2.1.9 OESP, 2.1.13 USoA balances reconciled to audited statements, 2.1.14 net metering, 2.1.16 LEAP, 2.1.17 large customers, 2.1.19 scorecard measures, 2.1.20 publicly traded status, 2.1.22 cyber security readiness, 2.2.1 Affiliate Relationships Code certification); quarterly generation connection data due on the last day of the second month after quarter end (2.1.15); CEO certification of the scorecard and MD&A (2.2.2); quarterly and annual certification by the CEO or RRR signing officer that filings are complete and accurate and that controls are adequate (2.2.3); immediate reporting of material load loss (2.1.18).

sources.title: Scorecard - Hydro Ottawa Limited (2017-2021) and 2021 Scorecard Management Discussion and Analysis
sources.supports: The scorecard page is dated August 31, 2022 and is followed by an 11-page utility-written Scorecard MD&A explaining each measure (service quality, customer satisfaction, safety, reliability, asset management, cost control, connection of renewable generation, financial ratios); a footnote notes a measure whose RRR filing requirement was removed in 2021; the utility commissioned a research firm for its public awareness of electrical safety survey.

assumptions: The unit of work is one return: about fifteen annual sections due April 30, the February market monitoring summary, four quarterly generation connection returns and the scorecard MD&A, which gives about 21 cases a year (1.75 a month). Certification is modelled once per return, although in practice one certification can cover several returns filed on the same date.
The OEB yearbook and scorecard are produced by the OEB from these returns; the utility's own scorecard work is the MD&A branch.
Branch shares by return type follow the section count in s1 and are not weighted by effort.
The OEB follow-up rate (7%) and the share of queries that lead to data revisions are estimates.
fte_on_process covers RRR returns only; the same analysts also prepare annual rate updates and deferral account work, which are separate processes.
